newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles settles dispute with Pacific Pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles settles dispute with Pacific Pipeline.

text.p: The city of Los Angeles agreed on Wednesday to drop its ongoing legal battle with the owners of Pacific Pipeline, a 132-mile line being built from central California to refineries south of the city.
"We are pleased to have resolved all issue with the City of Los Angeles," said Jim Shamas, Pacific Pipeline vice president.
Pacific, owned by Colorado-based Anshutz Corp, will carry down 130,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude oil from the prolific fields of San Joaquin Valley.
As part of the settlement, Pacific agreed to help the city make improvements on its emergency communications system and will provide computers to city neighborhoods where the line will run.
Opponents of the line, including some members of the city council, argued earthquakes could rupture the line, which will run through residential neighbohoods in Northeast Los Angeles.
As late as Februay, opponents had planned to challenge the construction on grounds it violated certain environmental laws. They also planned to appeal earlier court rulings.
Contruction began on the line earlier this year and is slated for completion by early next year.
